newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Lek sees 96 pre-tax steady, sales up.
newsitem.headline: Lek sees 96 pre-tax steady, sales up.

text.p: Slovenian pharmaceutical producer Lek said on Tuesday its 1996 pre-tax profit was roughly flat while sales increased four percent.
Company spokesman Simona Rodez Strucl said pre-tax profit was an estimated three billion tolars, compared with 2.9 billion in 1995. Sales rose four percent to 38 billion tolars ($255.0 million).
In 1996 some 73 percent of Lek's production was exported, mainly to neighbouring Croatia, U.S., Poland, Russia and Canada.
Lek's A issue share, which has drawn strong demand from foreign investors, has surged over 130 percent since it was listed on September 11. Strucl said 18.9 percent of shares were in foreign hands.
On Tuesday Lek's A issue shares were trading 3.41 percent down at 32,000 tolars on volume of 4,601 shares.
